output.brief:
Pay does not explain the departures. Our salaries sit in the same market band as the rest of the firm. The rival firm's band is £3–5k higher, not the £15k quoted. Most leavers took equal or lower pay. The billable-target rise applied to every group, and the other groups' attrition stayed normal. Ordinary market mobility doesn't fit either.

The departures are concentrated on Kestrel: 8 of 11 Kestrel associates resigned, against 1 of 13 who never worked on it. Every Kestrel associate was supervised by Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no other matter. So the heavy workload and his supervision can't be told apart in the records. Survey comments point to both: weekend work and humiliating late-night corrections. I can't say which one is driving the departures, or whether it's both.

Don't announce the £12k retention payment and close the review. It would spend about £228k on the wrong cause and leave the problem in place.

Next step: commission the confidential external interviews (about £9k, three weeks), designed to separate supervision from workload. Meanwhile, start tracking matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting. Decide on moving supervision or adding contract reviewers once the interviews are in. Kestrel's review phase runs to December 2026, so don't let the interviews drag on.
